intro: This is AaharOS, an order-to-audit system for a small South Indian snack factory. Every gram is traced, and every rupee is explained.
howto: The Instructions page gives two step-by-step routines: first the guided tour, then your own factory. Each one can be heard in English or Tamil.
tour-start: The guided tour walks through one working day. Each step says who does it, where to go, what to type, and the number you should see. Next opens only after the step is ticked as done.
t-purchase: Step two. The production supervisor buys sixty kilos of flour at forty-five rupees. The average cost becomes forty-three rupees thirteen paise a kilo.
tamil: தமிழ் அழுத்தினால், முழுச் செயலியும் குரல் வழிகாட்டியும் உடனே தமிழுக்கு மாறும்.
t-issue: Step three. Start a batch and issue forty kilos of flour, ten and a half litres of oil, and one point two kilos of spice.
t-output: Step four. Record one hundred and eighty-eight good packets. Oil is five percent over, and yield is six percent under, so both are flagged.
t-order-a: Step five. Salesman A orders one hundred and fifty packets on the phone, even without network.
t-invoice: Step six. The admin approves the order, raises the GST invoice of seven thousand eight hundred and seventy-five rupees, and dispatches the oldest batch first.
t-order-b: Step seven. Distributor B asks for one hundred and twenty packets, but only eighty-eight are available. The shortage of thirty-two is flagged.
t-payment: Step eight. Retailer A pays four thousand rupees, leaving three thousand eight hundred and seventy-five owed.
t-costs: Step nine. Labour and gas are added. The cost per good packet is thirty-one rupees fourteen paise.
t-brief: Step ten. The owner's morning brief ranks today's three actions by their rupee impact.
t-reports: Step eleven. The auditor downloads the month's registers, the GST summary, and the evidence pack.
t-finish: Step twelve. The sample-day check replays the whole day and checks twenty-six figures.
finish: The tour is finished. Now we create our own factory.
signup: A factory name, your name, an email, and a password. The new factory starts with the same opening stock, recipe and prices.
f-purchase: In our own factory the day begins. Sixty kilos of flour are received at forty-five rupees.
f-batch: The batch card previews every stock change before posting. Flour goes from one hundred and sixty to one hundred and twenty kilos.
f-output: One hundred and eighty-eight good packets are posted. Raw stock goes down, and finished stock goes up, automatically.
f-order-a: Salesman A orders one hundred and fifty packets for Retailer A.
f-order-b: Salesman B orders one hundred and twenty packets for Distributor B.
f-approve: The admin approves Retailer A against the stock that can really be promised.
f-short: Distributor B's card shows eighty-eight available and thirty-two short, with IGST, because Karnataka is another state.
f-invoice: The GST invoice. Seven thousand five hundred rupees taxable, plus CGST and SGST of one hundred eighty-seven fifty each.
f-dispatch: Dispatch takes fifty packets from the opening lot and one hundred from batch B zero zero one.
f-payment: A payment of four thousand rupees is recorded against the invoice.
f-costs: Run costs. Five thousand eight hundred and fifty-five rupees in total, thirty-one rupees fourteen paise per packet, and a margin of eighteen rupees eighty-six paise.
f-brief: The owner's morning brief, shown here in Tamil.
f-leaks: Where profit leaks. Four hundred and thirty-one rupees above standard, led by the yield loss.
f-gst: The GST summary matches the invoice, in the shape of GSTR-1.
f-check: And the sample-day check. Twenty-six of twenty-six correct. Every gram traced. Every rupee explained.
